headline: High: shared filesystem and broad egress create default risks of prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors between gpt-researcher and transformers.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: gpt-researcher reads files, runs browsers, and uses MCP; transformers can read/write files and run shell code. That creates a plausible shared-file or pipeline bridge where content from one can be treated as instructions by the other. No explicit provenance or isolation is documented for either agent.
conditions: IF the two agents exchange files through a shared workspace or stdin/stdout pipeline
IF either agent parses the other's generated text as instructions
mitigations: Separate their working directories
Disable automatic ingestion of generated documents as prompts
Add provenance tags to all exchanged files
Require manual review before passing outputs between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: gpt-researcher touches research queries, reports, local documents, citations, and images, while transformers processes text, audio, images, video, and multimodal data. Both have broad network egress and filesystem access, so sensitive local content can flow out through either agent's backend or APIs in default use.
conditions: IF either agent is given local documents containing sensitive data
IF outputs or intermediate files are sent to external APIs or hubs
mitigations: Restrict both agents to non-sensitive datasets
Block outbound network except approved endpoints
Redact secrets before file ingestion
Use separate service accounts and workspaces

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can read the filesystem, spawn subprocesses, install packages, and have broad network egress; transformers also writes files and executes shell commands. In a shared directory, concurrent writes and package changes can overwrite each other or corrupt state, and no locking mechanism is documented.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same directory or environment
IF package installation or file writes occur concurrently
mitigations: Run each agent in an isolated container
Use separate virtual environments
Mount read-only inputs and separate output dirs
Serialize package installation steps
Add file locks around shared mutable paths

D_cascading_error.rationale: gpt-researcher is a planner/execution/publisher pipeline that produces research reports and citations, and transformers can consume files and scripts. If transformers treats gpt-researcher's output as authoritative, errors or hallucinated citations can cascade into downstream processing or actions without verification.
conditions: IF transformers consumes gpt-researcher reports without independent verification
IF downstream scripts or model pipelines act on those reports
mitigations: Insert a verification step before reuse
Require source-link checks on citations
Keep generated reports read-only until reviewed
Log and diff all downstream transformations

E_compliance.rationale: gpt-researcher handles research queries, local documents, citations, and images, while transformers processes multimodal data and can write model or source files. If regulated or residency-bound content is placed into either agent, differing retention and hosting practices can create compliance gaps; the profiles do not document matching controls.
conditions: IF EU PII, PHI, or other regulated data is processed by either agent
IF retention or hosting requirements differ between the two deployments
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both agents
Document residency and retention settings
Use separate deployments for regulated workloads
Review vendor DPAs and logging defaults
